editorial:
Imagine being a stay-at-home mom who feels like she has no control over her own life. You meet Hunter, a woman who seems to have it all, but her husband and his family treat her like a child. She is pregnant and stuck in a fancy house where everyone tells her what to do. Things get weird when she starts feeling a strange urge to eat things that aren't food, like pebbles and pins. It starts small, but it quickly turns into a dangerous habit that makes you feel her stress and panic in every scene.

The acting is top-notch and makes the whole experience feel real. You will find yourself holding your breath during the scenes where she swallows sharp objects. The pacing is steady, though some might find the middle part a bit slow. If you like stories about people breaking free from bad situations, you will love this. It really makes the sharp visuals pop.
endingExplained: In the end, Hunter realizes her eating habit is a way to deal with her controlling husband. She decides she cannot live like this anymore. After a tense standoff, she finally stands up for herself and leaves her husband and his overbearing family behind. She chooses her own freedom over the fake perfect life she was forced to live. It is a happy ending because she finally takes back control of her body and her future.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about female empowerment.
